solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/three-divisors/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

1952. Three Divisors

Given an integer n, return true if n has exactly three positive divisors. Otherwise, return false.

An integer m is a divisor of n if there exists an integer k such that n = k * m.

Example 1:

Input: n = 2
Output: false
Explantion: 2 has only two divisors: 1 and 2.

Example 2:

Input: n = 4
Output: true
Explantion: 4 has three divisors: 1, 2, and 4.

Constraints:

    1 <= n <= 10^4
"""


class Solution:
    def isThree(self, n: int) -> bool:
        # A number has exactly three positive divisors if and only if it is a perfect square of a prime number.
        # So we check if n is a perfect square, and if its square root is prime.
        if n < 2:
            return False
        root = int(sqrt(n))
        if root * root != n:
            return False
        # Check if root is prime
        if root < 2:
            return False
        for i in range(2, int(sqrt(root)) + 1):
            if root % i == 0:
                return False
        return True


sol = Solution()

print(sol.isThree(2))  # False

assert sol.isThree(2) == False
assert sol.isThree(4) == True

assert sol.isThree(1) == False
assert sol.isThree(9) == True
assert sol.isThree(16) == False
assert sol.isThree(25) == True
assert sol.isThree(27) == False
assert sol.isThree(49) == True
assert sol.isThree(50) == False
assert sol.isThree(100) == False
assert sol.isThree(121) == True
assert sol.isThree(169) == True
assert sol.isThree(10**4) == False
assert sol.isThree(9999) == False
